title: What Makes a Banana Slightly Radioactive?

scenes.text: Did you know a single banana contains a measurable amount of radiation?

scenes.label: POTASSIUM‑40 ISOTOPES
scenes.text: Bananas are rich in potassium‑40, a naturally occurring radioactive isotope.

scenes.label: MEASURABLE DURATION
scenes.text: One banana delivers about 0.1 microsieverts—far below any health risk.

scenes.label: BENCHMARK UNIT
scenes.text: Scientists use “banana equivalents” to illustrate tiny radiation exposures in everyday life.

description: A banana’s glow isn’t a myth—tiny potassium‑40 atoms make it slightly radioactive. Learn the three key facts behind this tasty quirk. Hit follow for more everyday science mysteries!
